title: (No AI) Friends don’t let friends feed their data to AI agents
author: Janus Rose
content:
![Muse mascot with red eyes](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268808_None_of_Your_Friends_Consented_To_an_AI_Agent_CVirginia2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

There's a growing trend in the consumer tech world: gadgets [designed to spy on everything and everyone around you](https://www.theverge.com/tech/999889/spy-creep-tech-meta-glasses-apple-watches-surveillance), regardless of whether or not anyone else actually consented to it. Now, with the advent of "AI personal assistants" like Meta's Muse, you're being cheerfully asked not just to give up your own data, but also the information of your friends, family, the person you went on a Hinge date with five years ago - and virtually anyone else you've ever come in contact with.

Since Muse was released last month, the agent has already been downloaded millions of times and hit No. 1 on Apple's App Store. With the help of its creepy virtual av …

title: (No AI) How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops
author: Tom Warren
content:
![Windows logo on black background](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/08/STK109_WINDOWS_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Microsoft and Nvidia held a launch party for the first wave of RTX Spark laptops last week in San Francisco, where a new wave of AI PCs took center stage amid a packed crowd and a lively hands-on area. A day after the media event, I was invited to a quieter Nvidia event to hear a lot more about the new RTX Spark computing platform. While Nvidia's new laptops might look like regular Windows machines, the chips inside are Arm-based, instead of the traditional x64 architecture used by AMD and Intel. Combined with a powerful GPU, RTX Spark is designed for the future of AI, and it means a lot of work has gone into getting these laptops ready for …
